issues.description: The problem description text instructs students to implement addGuestStudents(String) (textual task), but the UML and the intended implementation use addGuestStudents(int). This mismatch in the parameter type for addGuestStudents will confuse students about which signature to implement and may cause compilation or test failures if they follow the textual description instead of the UML/template.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the parameter type consistent across the problem statement, template, UML and solution. Change the textual task in problem_statement.md from addGuestStudents(String) to addGuestStudents(int) (or update the UML/solution/template to use String if that was intended). Preferably use int to match the UML and solution implementation and update the task text accordingly.

issues.description: The problem text (task description) specifies addGuestStudents(String) while the UML diagram and the solution implementation define addGuestStudents(int). This mismatch in the method signature (parameter type) creates confusion about the expected input type and may lead students to implement the wrong signature and fail tests or compilation.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the task description with the UML and solution by changing the problem text to require addGuestStudents(int). Alternatively, if strings were intended, update the UML and solution to use addGuestStudents(String) consistently. Prefer the int parameter (number of students) to match domain semantics.
